title: Unpaid Meal Charge Policy of the School Nutrition Services Meal Account (USDA SP 46-2016)
content:
This is the district's written unpaid meal charge policy under USDA SP 46-2016 for every School Nutrition Services Meal Account.

1. **Charging a meal.** When the meal status allows a reimbursable meal to be charged, a reimbursable meal may be charged when the balance is not enough, until the balance reaches the charge limit of the campus level (the elementary, middle school or high school charge limit, read as a negative balance). Once the limit is reached the student is still served a reimbursable meal and it is charged, and no student is ever given an alternate meal or denied a meal.
2. **Other items.** A la carte items, second meals and milk bought alone are sold only when the account's balance covers them without falling below zero, for every status. The balance is every transaction on the account from opening up to the moment of the decision, negative balances carrying across school years: its deposits, voids and transfers in less its purchases, refunds, transfers out and returned deposits.
3. **Notices.** A low-balance notice is sent when a purchase leaves the balance at or below the low-balance threshold and still zero or above; a negative-balance notice is sent when the balance first falls below zero and again every 7 days (the negative-balance notice interval) while it stays below zero; a charge-limit-reached notice is sent on the day the limit is reached.
4. **Carry-forward and collection.** Unpaid meal charges carry into the next school year on the same account, a year-end collection notice is sent for a balance still negative after the last instructional day, and no fee, interest or penalty is ever added to unpaid meal charges.
5. **Deposits.** Any deposit is applied to unpaid meal charges first, because it simply raises the balance.

## Decision table at the register

| Purchase | Balance after the purchase | Sold? |
|---|---|---|
| reimbursable meal, status allows charging | at or above the negative charge limit | yes, charged |
| reimbursable meal, status allows charging | limit already reached | yes, served and charged |
| a la carte item, second meal or milk alone | zero or above | yes |
| a la carte item, second meal or milk alone | below zero | no |

## Notice illustration (hypothetical)

An account at 2.00 buys a 3.10 lunch and stands at 1.10 below zero: a negative-balance notice goes out that day and, if the balance is still below zero, again seven calendar days later. A deposit of 20.00 the next week first clears the 1.10 owed simply by raising the balance to 18.90.
